kzz7yh-f125549-d1e103.summary: Literal notes on II d.44. 'Bad will is not from God' means the act of bad will, insofar as it is bad, is not from God. The Apostle (Romans 13) speaks of secular power, kings and princes, who must not be resisted in what pertains to their power by right, as Lombard's following words show: obedience is owed in tributes and the like.
claims: The act of bad will is not from God insofar as it is bad.
Non-resistance to secular rulers holds only within their rightful power.

kzz7yh-f125549-d1e132.summary: Objection: the gloss on Apocalypse 2 says an archbishop does not presume to lay hands on a bishop's subjects without the bishop, so the higher superior is not always obeyed more.
claims: An archbishop cannot act on a bishop's subjects without the bishop (objection).

kzz7yh-f125549-d1e141.summary: Reply: an archbishop, though superior to a bishop, lacks full power over the bishop and his subjects, so those subjects owe more obedience to their bishop except in certain cases. But a superior prelate with fullness of power over subjects, such as the Pope, is always to be obeyed more than a lower prelate. Since God has fullness of power over all, he is to be obeyed most of all and perseveringly; the commentary on Book II closes with a prayer that Christ lead us to salvation through persevering obedience.
claims: Obedience to superiors depends on their having plenary jurisdiction.
The Pope, with fullness of power, is always to be obeyed over lower prelates.
God, having fullness of power over all, is to be obeyed most of all.

kzz7yh-f125549.summary: Circa litteram on II d.44 and closing of Book II. Richard specifies that a bad act of will is not from God insofar as it is bad, and that Romans 13's non-resistance concerns secular rulers acting within their rightful power, such as in tributes. He then explains hierarchical obedience by jurisdiction: an archbishop lacks plenary power over a bishop's subjects, but a superior with fullness of power, the Pope, is always obeyed above lower prelates, and God, with fullness of power over all, is to be obeyed most of all and perseveringly. A prayer for salvation through obedience closes the book.
claims: The Pope's fullness of power ranks his commands over lower prelates.
God is to be obeyed above all.
